paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise indicates, references to "Flowserve," "the Company" and such words as "we," "our" and "us" include Flowserve Corporation and its subsidiaries.

Flowserve's goal is to create extraordinary flow control solutions to make the world better for everyone. We are a world-leading manufacturer and aftermarket service provider of comprehensive flow control systems. We develop and manufacture precision-engineered flow control equipment integral to the movement, control and protection of the flow of materials in our customers' critical processes. Our product portfolio of pumps, valves, seals, automation and aftermarket services supports global infrastructure industries, including energy, chemical, power generation and general, which includes water management and pharmaceuticals, where our products and services enable customers to achieve their goals. Through our manufacturing platform and global network of Quick Response Centers ("QRCs"), we offer a broad array of aftermarket equipment services, such as installation, advanced diagnostics and turnkey maintenance programs.

Flowserve has a clear growth strategy as we transform our operations to better meet our customers' needs. Our overarching strategic objectives are to remain a global leader in the flow control industry and capitalize on growth through our traditional end markets as well as through specifically identified growth areas, such as the nuclear, energy transition and power generation markets. We seek to be recognized by our customers as the most trusted brand of flow control technology in terms of reliability and quality, which we believe will help maximize shareholder value.

In pursuit of these objectives, we maintain a strategic plan that takes a balanced approach to integrating both short-term and long-term initiatives and accelerates growth through three key areas: diversification, decarbonization, and digitization (the "3D Strategy"). The goal of our 3D Strategy is to utilize our leadership in the flow control industry, and through our commitment to research and development ("R&D"), create innovative products and solutions which address the emerging climate and environmental issues that our customers face. In addition, the Flowserve Business System helps guide the enterprise on incorporating best in class operational practices within the following categories: People Excellence, Operational Excellence, Portfolio Excellence, Commercial Excellence, and Innovation Excellence (the "Flowserve Business System"). We believe that our 3D Strategy, improved execution through our operating model and the Flowserve Business System, and continued innovation efforts will drive long-term revenue growth and profit expansion. For further discussion of our operating model, see the Executive Overview in "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 ("Annual Report").

We are diversifying our traditional end markets to create a more balanced and less cyclical portfolio with a focus in the following end markets: nuclear, power generation, water, specialty chemicals, and new vacuum and seal technologies. With the goal of supporting our customers today and in the future as they transition to new energy sources, we focus on several elements to create a balanced and diverse portfolio based on cleaner sources of energy, including: (i) re-engaging our offerings with market participants in areas such as nuclear, power generation, water, specialty chemicals, and other general industries where we maintain strong capabilities; (ii) increasing our exposure to end markets offering long-term outsized growth potential; and (iii) maintaining and growing our vacuum technology that supports chemical processing and advanced industrial manufacturing.

We are supporting our customers through their energy transitions. Countries and corporations around the world continue to invest in various methods and solutions to help achieve their climate and emission reduction goals. Our decarbonization strategy focuses on several areas and seeks to address the effects of climate change through our innovative portfolio of flow control solutions, including: (i) continuing to develop our products and services that can be utilized in our customers' carbon reduction efforts; (ii) providing overall product and solution offerings to help customers' energy transition efforts in energy efficiency, carbon reduction, and operational cost mitigation; and (iii) maintaining and improving our technologies already available in nuclear, liquefied natural gas ("LNG"), hydrogen, carbon capture, and renewables. The Flowserve Energy Advantage Program provides a holistic flow control approach aimed at helping

operators reach their carbon reduction goals and lower total cost of ownership. The program provides customers with Flowserve's engineering expertise, a systematic data-driven evaluation process and a complete offering of products and services that can help increase energy efficiency through optimization of pump and valve power consumption, reduce carbon emissions, improve plant productivity and reliability, and provide operational cost savings.

We are leveraging technology and data to improve our, and our customers', operations. With a goal of digitizing our existing installed base and new original equipment, we focus on several efforts to help our customers digitize their operations, including: (i) implementing RedRaven, our proprietary Industrial Internet of Things ("IIoT") solution for equipment monitoring, to improve customers' internal operations; (ii) supporting customer sites across a diverse set of industry applications; and (iii) utilizing RedRaven to monitor existing assets, predict costly downtime in critical assets, and optimize flow loop operations.

Our investments in Flowserve solutions focus on developing and scaling offerings that improve energy efficiency and uptime, reduce total cost-of-ownership, and enhance safety for our end-users. Through our Energy Advantage Program, we have invested in a dedicated team, proprietary analysis tools and new business models to identify and implement energy-efficiency improvements across flow control systems.

In addition, we continue to advance our capabilities and technology position in the rapidly developing asset health market. Over the past several years, we have continued to both invest and partner in this space to expand remote monitoring solutions and advanced equipment diagnostics to provide remote asset management and related services and capabilities for our end-user customers. Our solution, RedRaven, includes delivering intelligent "edge" devices, advanced networking infrastructure, secure communication and security protocols, secure data management, and remote monitoring and reporting for our customers.

None of these newly developed products or services required the investment of a material amount of our assets or were otherwise material to our business. We expect to increase our R&D focus in the above areas.

Flowserve Corporation was created in 1997 through the merger of two leading fluid motion and control companies — BW/IP and Durco International. Under the name of a predecessor entity, we were incorporated in the State of New York on May 1, 1912, but some of our heritage product brand names date back to our founding in 1790. We have evolved through organic growth and strategic acquisitions, and our over 230-year history of Flowserve heritage brands serves as the foundation for the breadth and depth of our products and services today.

We sell our products and services to over 10,000 customers, including some of the world's leading engineering, procurement, and construction ("EPC") firms, original equipment manufacturers, distributors, and end users. Our products and services are used in several distinct industries having a broad geographic reach. We revised the end market categories for bookings during the first quarter of 2025 to better reflect the end markets of our customers and better align with Flowserve's strategic focus. All bookings by industry amounts discussed below, including the comparative periods, have been reclassified from five categories (i.e., oil and gas, chemical, power generation, water management and general industries) to four categories (i.e., energy, chemical, power generation, and general industries) to conform to our current classification of end markets. paragraphs: Please carefully consider the following discussion of material factors, events, and uncertainties that make an investment in our securities risky. If any of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below or elsewhere in this Annual Report materialize, our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, reputation, prospects, or stock price could be materially adversely affected. While we believe all known material risks are disclosed, additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently deem immaterial, may also materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, reputation, prospects, or stock price. The disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past. Because of the risk factors discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report and in other filings we make with the SEC, as well as other variables affecting our operating results, past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance, historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods and actual results could differ materially from those projected in the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report.

Our business depends on our customers' levels of capital investment and maintenance expenditures, which in turn are affected by numerous factors, including changes in the state of domestic and global economies, global energy demand, and the liquidity cyclicality and condition of global credit and capital markets, which have impacted and which could continue to impact the ability or willingness of our customers to invest in our products and services and adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flow.

Demand for most of our products and services depends on the level of new capital investment and planned maintenance expenditures by our customers. The level of capital expenditures by our customers depends, in turn, on general economic conditions, availability of credit, economic conditions within their respective industries and expectations of future market behavior. Additionally, volatility in commodity prices can negatively affect the level of these activities and can result in postponement of capital spending decisions or the delay or cancellation of existing orders. The ability of our customers to finance capital investment and maintenance is also affected by factors independent of the conditions in their industry, such as the condition of global credit and capital markets.

The businesses of many of our customers, particularly energy companies, chemical companies and general industrial companies, are to varying degrees cyclical and have experienced periodic downturns. Our customers in these industries, particularly those whose demand for our products and services is primarily profit-driven, tend to delay large capital projects, including expensive maintenance and upgrades, during economic downturns. For example, our chemical customers generally tend to reduce their spending on capital investments and operate their facilities at lower levels in a soft economic environment, which reduces demand for our products and services. An economic slowdown or recession in the United States or in any other country that significantly affects the supply of or demand for oil or natural gas could negatively impact our operations and therefore adversely affect our results. Additionally, fluctuating energy demand forecasts and lingering uncertainty concerning commodity pricing, specifically the price of oil, have caused, and may in the future cause, our customers to be more conservative in their capital planning, reducing demand for our products and services. Reduced demand for our products and services from time to time results in the delay or cancellation of existing orders or leads to excess manufacturing capacity, which unfavorably impacts our absorption of fixed manufacturing costs. This reduced demand has in the past and may continue in the future to also erode average selling prices in our industry. Any of these results could continue to adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Volatile regional and global economic conditions stemming from public health emergencies, such as outbreaks of epidemics, pandemics, and contagious diseases, including actions taken by governments in response, could in the future cause a substantial curtailment of business activities (including the decrease in demand for a broad variety of goods and services), weakened economic conditions, supply chain disruptions, significant economic uncertainty, and volatility in the financial and commodity markets, including global volatility in supply and demand for energy, may precipitate and aggravate many of the factors described above, and could cause these factors to adversely impact our operations and financial performance as well as those of many of our customers and suppliers.

Additionally, our customers sometimes delay capital investment and maintenance even during favorable conditions in their industries or markets. Despite these favorable conditions, the general health of global credit and capital markets and our customers' ability to access such markets impacts investments in large capital projects, including necessary maintenance and upgrades. In addition, the liquidity and financial position of our customers impacts capital investment decisions and their ability to pay in full and/or on a timely basis. Any of these factors, whether individually or in the aggregate, could have a material adverse effect on our customers and, in turn, our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

paragraphs: We have seen growth from the end markets we serve and continue to focus on our strategic plan that takes a balanced approach to integrating both short-term and long-term initiatives and aims to accelerate growth through three key areas: diversification, decarbonization, and digitization, the "3D Strategy." Our strategy is expected to deliver sustainable growth, while the Flowserve Business System is expected to unlock gains in organizational and operational efficiency. The current macroeconomic environment is dynamic and uncertainty exists given the current geopolitical climate and continued trade policy actions, including higher import tariffs in a number of countries in which we operate, the potential implementation

of modified or new tariffs and related retaliatory actions. We plan to leverage our global footprint, expansive manufacturing network, flexible supply chain and ability to incorporate tariff impacts into pricing decisions to minimize the economic impact of this uncertainty to our business. We will continue to monitor and manage macroeconomic trends and uncertainties, including inflationary and recessionary pressures resulting from the ongoing tariffs and geopolitical climate; however, with our strong backlog, improved execution and recent acquisitions activity, we expect to deliver annual revenue growth in 2026.

Our bookings were $4.7 billion during the year ended December 31, 2025. Because a booking represents a contract that can be, in certain circumstances, modified or canceled, and can include varying lengths between the time of booking and the time of revenue recognition, there is no guarantee that bookings will result in comparable revenues or otherwise be indicative of future results. Assuming a positive general macroeconomic environment and continued supportive environments in our end markets, we expect full-year bookings growth in 2026.

On October 10, 2024, we entered into the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, which includes a $800.0 million Revolving Credit Facility and $500.0 million Term Loan. On December 31, 2025, we had $992.7 million of fixed-rate Senior Notes outstanding. We expect our interest expense in 2026 will be relatively consistent with amounts incurred in 2025. Our results of operations may also be impacted by unfavorable foreign currency exchange rate movements. See "Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk" of this Annual Report.

We expect to generate sufficient cash from operations and have sufficient capacity under our Senior Credit Facility to fund any working capital, capital expenditures, dividend payments, share repurchases, debt payments and pension plan contributions in 2026. The amount of cash generated or consumed by working capital is dependent on our level of revenues, customer cash advances, backlog, customer-driven delays and other factors. We will seek to improve our working capital utilization, with a particular focus on improving the management of accounts receivable and inventory. In 2026, our cash flows for investing activities will be focused on strategic initiatives, information technology infrastructure, general upgrades and cost reduction opportunities and we currently estimate capital expenditures to be between $90 million and $100 million, before consideration of any acquisition activity. We currently anticipate that our contributions to our non-U.S. pension plans will be approximately $3 million in 2026, excluding direct benefits paid. We have no obligation to make contributions to our U.S. pension plans in 2025, but have authorization for contributions up to $10 million.

The following is the discussion and analysis of changes in the financial condition and results of operations for fiscal year December 31, 2025 compared to fiscal year 2024. The discussion and analysis of changes in the financial condition and results of operations for fiscal year 2024 compared to fiscal year 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K may be found in Part II, "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025.

Throughout this discussion of our results of operations, we discuss the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates. We have calculated currency effects on operations by translating current year results on a monthly basis at prior year exchange rates for the same periods.

As discussed in Note 2, "Acquisitions," to our consolidated financial statements included in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report, effective October 15, 2024, we acquired for inclusion in FCD, all of the equity interests of MOGAS Industries, Inc., MOGAS Real Estate LLC and MOGAS Systems & Consulting LLC (such entities collectively, "MOGAS"). We incurred $12.8 million in acquisition and integration related costs for fiscal year December 31, 2025 associated with the acquisition which are included within selling, general and administrative expense ("SG&A") and cost of sales ("COS") in our consolidated statements of income. A full year of MOGAS operating results are included within the consolidated statement of income for the period ended December 31, 2025.

Our realignment activities are implemented in phases. We currently anticipate a total investment of approximately $93 million in the 2025 Realignment Programs that have been evaluated and initiated, of which $17 million is estimated to be non-cash. We are evaluating the annualized cost savings expected to be achieved upon completion of the activities of the 2025 Realignment Programs that have been identified and initiated to date. Actual savings could vary from expected savings. There are certain remaining realignment activities that are currently being evaluated, but have not yet been approved and therefore are not included in the above anticipated total investment or estimated savings.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有所指，否則提及 "Flowserve"、"the Company" 及其他如 "we"、"our" 和 "us" 之詞彙，均包含 Flowserve Corporation 及其子公司。

Flowserve 的目標是創造卓越的流量控制解決方案，以讓世界對所有人變得更好。我們是全球領先的流量控制系統製造商與後市場服務供應商。我們開發與製造精準工程設計的流量控制設備，這些設備對客戶關鍵流程中物質的流動、控制與保護至關重要。我們的產品組合包括泵、閥門、密封件、自動化與後市場服務，支持全球基礎設施產業，包括能源、化工、發電與一般產業，包括水管理與製藥產業，其中我們的產品與服務協助客戶達成其目標。透過我們的製造平台與全球 Quick Response Centers（"QRCs"）網路，我們提供廣泛的後市場設備服務，例如安裝、先進診斷與整體維護方案。
Flowserve 有明確的成長策略，我們正在轉型作業，以更好地符合客戶需求。我們的整體戰略目標是維持流量控制產業的全球領導地位，並透過傳統終端市場以及特定識別的成長領域，例如核能、能源轉型與發電市場，來把握成長機會。我們致力於被客戶視為最值得信賴的流量控制科技品牌，以可靠與品質為準，我們相信這將有助於最大化股東價值。

為達成這些目標，我們維持一個戰略計畫，以平衡的方式整合短期與長期的計畫，並透過三個關鍵領域加速成長：多元化、減碳化與數位化（"3D 策略"）。我們 3D 策略的目標是運用我們在流量控制產業的領導地位，並透過我們對研究與發展（"R&D"）的承諾，創造創新產品與解決方案，以應對客戶所面臨的 emerging 氣候與環境問題。此外，Flowserve 商業系統協助企業在以下類別中納入最佳作業實踐：人才卓越、作業卓越、產品組合卓越、商業卓越與創新卓越（"Flowserve 商業系統"）。我們相信，我們的 3D 策略、透過我們作業模式與 Flowserve 商業系統提升的執行效率，以及持續的創新努力，將推動長期營業收入成長與獲利擴張。有關我們作業模式的進一步討論，請參閱本年度報表（"Annual Report"）中 "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" 所包含的執行總覽部分，該年度報表為 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的 Form 10-K 年度報告。

我們正在多元化傳統終端市場，以建立更平衡且較少週期性的組合，重點在以下終端市場：核能、發電、水、特殊化學品與新真空與密封技術。為支持客戶今日與未來的轉型，我們專注於幾個要素，以建立基於較清潔能源來源的平衡與多樣化組合，包括：(i) 重新與市場參與者合作，例如核能、發電、水、特殊化學品及其他一般產業，我們在這些領域擁有強大能力；(ii) 增加我們在提供長期高成長潛力終端市場的曝光度；以及 (iii) 優化與成長我們的真空技術，以支持化學處理與先進工業製造。

我們正在協助客戶進行能源轉型。全球各國與企業持續投資於各種方法與解決方案，以協助達成其氣候與減排目標。我們的減碳策略著重於幾個領域，並致力於透過我們創新流量控制解決方案來應對氣候變遷的影響，包括：(i) 繼續開發可用於客戶減碳努力的產品與服務；(ii) 提供全面的產品與解決方案，協助客戶的能源轉型努力，包括能源效率、減碳與運營成本降低；以及 (iii) 優化與改善我們在核能、液化天然氣（"LNG"）、氫氣、碳捕捉與可再生能源領域已有的技術。Flowserve 能源優勢計畫提供一個全面的流量控制方法，旨在協助
運營者達成其減碳目標並降低總擁有成本。該計畫為客戶提供 Flowserve 的工程專業知識、系統化的數據驅動評估流程，以及完整的產品與服務組合，以協助提高能源效率，透過泵與閥門的電力消耗最佳化，減少碳排放，提高工廠生產力與可靠性，並提供運營成本節省。

我們正在利用科技與數據來改善我們與客戶的作業。我們的目標是數位化我們現有的安裝基礎與新的原裝設備，我們專注於幾個努力，以協助客戶數位化其作業，包括：(i) 實施 RedRaven，我們專有的工業互聯網（"IIoT"）解決方案，用於設備監測，以改善客戶的內部作業；(ii) 支援客戶在多樣產業應用中的現場；以及 (iii) 利用 Red、Raven 監測現有資產，預測關鍵資產的高成本停機時間，並最佳化流量迴路作業。
本公司對 Flowserve 解決方案的投資重點在於開發與擴展能提升能源效率與運作時間、降低總擁有成本，並提升終端用戶安全性的產品與服務。透過我們的 Energy Advantage Program，我們已投資專屬團隊、專利分析工具與新商業模式，以識別並落實於流體控制系統中的能源效率改進方案。
此外，我們持續進步在快速發展的資產健康市場中的能力與技術地位。過去幾年，我們持續投資並與該領域的夥伴合作，以擴展遠端監測解決方案與先進設備診斷技術，為終端用戶客戶提供遠端資產管理及相關服務與能力。我們的解決方案 RedRaven 包含提供智慧 "edge" 裝置、先進網路基礎設施、安全通訊與安全協議、安全資料管理，以及遠端監測與報告服務。
上述新開發的產品或服務均未需要本公司投入重大資產，亦未對本公司業務產生重大影響。我們預期會在上述領域增加研發的投入重點。

Flowserve Corporation 於 1997 年透過合併兩家領先的流體運動與控制公司 — BW/IP 與 Durco International 而成立。以前身公司的名稱，我們於 1912 年 5 月 1 日在紐約州註冊成立，但部分我們的歷史產品品牌名稱可追溯至 1790 年的創立時期。我們透過內生成長與戰略收購而持續進化，我們超過 230 年的 Flowserve 歷史品牌基礎，奠定了我們目前產品與服務的廣度與深度。

我們將產品與服務銷售給超過 10,000 家客戶，包括一些全球知名的工程、採購與建設（"EPC"）公司、原廠設備製造商、經銷商與終端用戶。我們的產品與服務應用於幾個不同的產業，具有廣泛的地理分佈。我們於 2025 年第一季重新調整了終端市場分類，以更符合客戶的終端市場特性，並與 Flowserve 的戰略重點更一致。以下所討論的各產業銷售訂單金額，包括與前一時期的比較，均已從五個類別（即石油與天然氣、化工、電力發電、水管理與一般產業）重新歸類為四個類別（即能源、化工、電力發電與一般產業），以符合我們目前的終端市場分類方式。我們 2025 年、2024 年與 2023 年的銷售訂單金額分別為 47 億美元、47 億美元與 43 億美元。我們 2025 年、2024 年與 2023 年的產業銷售訂單組成如下：

paragraphs: 我們觀察到所服務的終端市場出現成長，並持續著重於我們的戰略計畫，該計畫以平衡的方式整合短期與長期的計畫，並旨在透過三個關鍵領域加速成長：多元化、減碳與數位化，即所謂的 "3D Strategy"。我們的策略預期將帶來可持續的成長，同時 Flowserve 商業系統預期將提升組織與運營效率。目前總體經濟環境動態且不確定性存在，這是因為當前的國際政治局勢以及持續的貿易政策行動，包括在若干我們營運國家提高進口關稅，以及潛在的新關稅或相關報復行動。我們計畫利用我們的全球據點、廣泛的製造網路、靈活的供應鏈以及將關稅影響納入定價決策的能力，以減少此不確定性對我們業務的經濟影響。我們將持續監測與管理總體經濟趨勢與不確定性，包括因持續關稅與國際政治局勢而產生的通貨膨脹與經濟衰退壓力；然而，憑藉我們強勁的訂單存量、改善的執行效率與近期的併購活動，我們預期將在 2026 年實現年度營業收入成長。
我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年期間的訂單金額為 47 億美元。因為訂單代表一份契約，該契約在某些情況下可能被修改或取消，且可能包含從訂單時間到收入確認時間之間的不確定時間長度，因此無法保證訂單會導致相當於收入或預示未來結果。假設總體經濟環境為正面，且我們終端市場的環境持續支持，我們預期 2026 年全年訂單金額將成長。
本公司於2025年12月31日財務年度的訂單金額為4.7十億美元。由於訂單代表一份契約，於特定情況下可能被修改或取消，且訂單與收入認列之間的時間間隔可能不一，因此無法保證訂單會產生相當於收入或反映未來結果。假設總體經濟環境持續正面，且我們終端市場的支撐環境持續，我們預期2026年全年訂單金額將成長。

於 2024 年 10 月 10 日，本公司與對方簽訂第二修正並重述信用協議，包含 800.0 百萬美元的循環信貸融資及 500.0 百萬美元的定期貸款。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司有 992.7 百萬美元的固定利率高級債券尚未償還。本公司預期 2026 年的利息支出將與 2025 年的支出大致相當。本公司營運成果也可能受到不利外幣匯率變動的影響。請參閱本年度報告之 "第 7A 項 有關市場風險之量化及質化揭露"。

我們預期將從營運中產生足夠的現金，並在2026年擁有足夠的資金來源及高階信貸融資能力，以支應任何營運資金、資本支出、股息支付、股票回購、債務償還及退休金計畫提撥。營運資金產生或消耗的金額取決於我們的營收水準、客戶現金預付款、待交付訂單、客戶驅動的延遲及其他因素。我們將致力於改善營運資金的運用效率，特別著重於應收帳款及存貨的管理。2026年，我們投資活動的現金流將聚焦於戰略性計畫、資訊科技基礎建設、一般性升級及成本削減機會，目前我們預估資本支出將介於90 百萬美元至100 百萬美元之間，不考慮任何併購活動。目前我們預期2026年對非美國退休金計畫的提撥將約為3 百萬美元，不包含直接支付的福利金額。我們在2025年沒有義務對美國退休金計畫進行提撥，但有權進行最高達10 百萬美元的提撥。

以下為財務狀況及營運成果在 2025 年財務年度（截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日）與 2024 年財務年度的變動情形之討論與分析。2024 年財務年度與 2023 年財務年度財務狀況及營運成果變動情形之討論與分析，未包含於本 Form 10-K 中者，可於我們 2024 年財務年度（截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日）的年度報告 Form 10-K，於 Part II，"Item 7. 管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析" 中找到，該報告已於 2025 年 2 月 26 日向 SEC 提交。
在本報告中對我們營運成果的討論中，我們會說明外幣匯率波動的影響。我們透過將當年結果以去年同期匯率換算，按月計算營運的匯率影響。

如附註 2「收購」所述，包含於本年度報告「項目 8. 財務報表及補充資料」中的合併財務報表，自 2024 年 10 月 15 日起，我們收購 MOGAS Industries, Inc.、MOGAS Real Estate LLC 與 MOGAS Systems & Consulting LLC 全部股權（這些實體合稱為「MOGAS」），並將其納入 FCD。我們於 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度中，因收購產生與整合相關費用為 1,280 萬美元，此費用包含於我們合併損益表中的營銷、一般及行政費用（"SG&A"）與銷售成本（"COS"）。2025 年 12 月 31 日結止期間的合併損益表中，已包含 MOGAS 全年的營運成果。
本公司重整活動分階段進行。目前預計2025年重整計畫總投資約為9300萬美元，其中已評估並啟動的計畫預計有1700萬美元為非現金支出。本公司正在評估已識別並啟動的2025年重整計畫完成後預期實現的年度成本節省。實際節省金額可能與預期節省金額有所差異。尚有部分重整活動目前仍在評估中，但尚未獲得批准，因此未包含於上述預計總投資或預估節省金額中。

paragraphs: 請謹慎考量下列有關重大因素、事件及不確定性之討論，這些因素、事件及潛在狀況使投資本公司證券具有風險。若任何上述因素、事件及潛在狀況實現，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、聲譽、前景或股票價格造成重大不利影響。雖然我們認為所有已知的重大風險均已揭露，但尚有其他風險及不確定性，可能尚未為我們所知或目前認為不重要，亦可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、聲譽、前景或股票價格造成重大不利影響。本節之揭露反映我們對未來可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響因素之信念與意見。對過往事件之參考僅為範例，並非完整清單，亦非表示這些因素是否已於過往發生。由於本年度報告中所討論之風險因素及其他因素，以及影響本公司營運結果之其他變數，過往財務表現可能無法作為未來表現之可靠指標，歷史趨勢亦不應用以預測未來期間之結果或趨勢，實際結果可能與本年度報告中所含之預測性陳述有重大差異。
本公司業務依賴客戶之資本投資及維護支出水平，而此等水平又受多項因素影響，包括國內與全球經濟狀態之變化、全球能源需求、以及全球信貸與資本市場之流動性週期性與狀況，這些因素已影響並可能繼續影響客戶投資本公司產品與服務之能力或意願，進而對本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流造成不利影響。
大多數本公司產品與服務之需求取決於客戶之新資本投資及預計維護支出水平。客戶之資本支出水平又取決於一般經濟條件、信貸可得性、其產業之經濟條件及對未來市場行為之預期。此外，商品價格波動可能對這些活動之水平產生負面影響，並導致資本支出決策延後或現有訂單之延遲或取消。客戶之資本投資與維護之融資能力亦受與其產業條件無關之因素影響，例如全球信貸與資本市場之狀況。

許多本公司客戶之業務，特別是能源公司、化學公司及一般工業公司，不同程度地具有週期性，並曾經歷週期性衰退。這些產業之客戶，特別是那些對本公司產品與服務之需求主要由利潤驅動之客戶，在經濟衰退期間傾向延後大型資本項目，包括昂貴之維護與升級。例如，本公司化學客戶通常在經濟環境較弱時減少資本投資支出，並以較低水平運作其設施，這會減少對本公司產品與服務之需求。美國或其他國家之經濟減速或衰退，若對石油或天然氣之供給或需求造成重大影響，可能對本公司營運造成負面影響，進而對本公司營運結果造成不利影響。此外，能源需求預測之波動及對商品價格，特別是石油價格之不確定性，已導致並可能在未來導致客戶在資本規劃上更加保守，減少對本公司產品與服務之需求。偶爾減少對本公司產品與服務之需求，會導致現有訂單之延遲或取消，或導致過度製造能力，這會對本公司固定製造成本之吸收產生不利影響。此減少之需求過去已並可能繼續對本公司產業之平均銷售價格造成影響。任何上述結果都可能繼續對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流造成不利影響。
由公共衛生緊急事件，例如傳染病、疫情及傳染性疾病爆發，以及政府所採取之行動所引發之區域及全球經濟條件波動，未來可能導致商業活動大幅減少（包括對廣泛商品與服務之需求減少）、經濟條件惡化、供應鏈中斷、重大經濟不確定性，以及財務與商品市場之波動，包括全球能源供應與需求之波動，可能引發並加劇上述許多因素，並可能對本公司營運及財務表現，以及許多客戶與供應商造成不利影響。
此外，本公司客戶有時即使在產業或市場條件有利之情況下，也會延後資本投資與維護。儘管這些條件有利，全球信貸與資本市場之整體健康狀況及客戶取得這些市場之能力，仍會影響對大型資本項目，包括必要之維護與升級之投資。此外，客戶之流動性與財務狀況會影響資本投資決策及其支付全額或及時付款之能力。任何上述因素，無論個別或整體，都可能對客戶造成重大不利影響，進而對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流造成影響。
